body: Census of lender candidates incl. merged/failed lenders (LVB, DHFL via Piramal Finance page, Reliance Capital, Reliance Home Finance, SREI, merged PSU banks chained into acquirers). n=107 company-snapshots (64 companies). P(>=3x) 11.2% [5.1-18.3], P(<=0.5x) 25.2% [17.0-33.3], P(blow-up) 27.1% [17.9-36.5], permanent blow-up 19.6% [11.9-28.0], median multiple 1.04x [0.84-1.62]. Start 2016: 3.8%/42.3%/34.6%; start 2018: 18.2%/9.1%/20.0%. Banks: 3.6% >=3x (no private bank tripled); NBFC/HFC: 19.6% >=3x but 33% blow-up. Versus India non-financial same windows: half the triple rate, double the halving rate, ~1.8x the blow-up rate. Survivors-only would say 15%/19%/20%. Gaps: 2 start dates in one credit cycle; YES Bank and Indiabulls Housing above the band; IL&FS/PMC unlisted; Syndicate Bank excluded (broken series); name-keyword frame misses no-keyword dead lenders; price only. Added to tools/decision/base_rates.json v3 as india_lender_1000_20000cr_5y; decision_card v1.5 auto-selects it for lenders. On UTKARSHBNK the model tails (21%/15%) are now below the class, so its w=0.3 note is stale.
title: India lender 5-year base-rate class (banks/SFBs/NBFCs/HFCs, mcap Rs 1,000-20,000 cr, T=2016/2018): P(>=3x) 11%, P(<=0.5x) 25%, blow-up 27% (permanent 20%), median 1.04x
